newsitem.title: ALBANIA: SOCCER-TIRANA WIN ALBANIAN TITLE AFTER LEADERS PENALISED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TIRANA WIN ALBANIAN TITLE AFTER LEADERS PENALISED.

text.p: Tirana were awarded the 1996-97 Albanian league title on Tuesday after rivals Flamurtari were docked four points, fined heavily and had two coaches suspended for two years.
Flamurtari walked off the pitch 15 minutes into the second half of their decisive and politically-charged match against Tirana last Sunday after having a penalty disallowed with Tirana leading 1-0.
The Vlore team had been two points ahead of Tirana going into the match.
The Albanian soccer federation gave Tirana a 2-0 victory for their 17th title.
A federation statement said Flamurtari were docked four points, fined 100,000 leks (approximately $600) and coaches Latif Gjondeda and Anesti Arapi were suspended.
Police were forced to intervene at the match when Flamurtari supporters smashed windows and seats in Tirana's Qemal Stafa stadium.

Flamurtari's home town, the southern port of Vlore, was the cradle for violent protests against the Tirana government earlier this year which led to new elections and President Sali Berisha's resignation last month.
The 1996-97 Albanian championship was suspended in February due to armed civil unrest in the Balkan country, although no matches had been played since December.
The league resumed 10 days ago in a six-team play-off after the government promised to guarantee security in the four stadiums chosen to host matches.
The new season is scheduled to begin on September 13.
The cloud over the league season could have further ramifications, with FIFA due to decide this week whether a September 10 World Cup qualifier against Northern Ireland can be played in Tirana.
Albanian home matches earlier in the year against Germany and the Ukraine were played in Spain.
"This incident is very bad for us. We really want to play our home qualifier at home," said national coach Astrit Hafizi.
Albanian clubs have been suspended by European body UEFA from all 1997-98 European cup competitions.
